source: Google Research: Centralized vs. Independent Agent Coordination (Jan 2026)
summary: Google study of 180 agent configurations found centralized coordination kept error amplification to 4.4x vs 17.2x for independent parallel agents. Validates sequential deterministic orchestration.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — validates AgentForge's existing design choice of sequential determinism; no gap to close

summary: Microsoft merged AutoGen and Semantic Kernel into a unified Agent Framework SDK reaching 1.0 GA in April 2026 (Python and .NET). AutoGen entered maintenance mode October 2025.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — Python/.NET SDK, not TypeScript; architectural patterns like actor-style agents interesting but no direct integration gap

source: CrewAI 2026 updates: Cognitive Memory, Crew Studio, A2A (v1.15.18)
summary: CrewAI shipped Cognitive Memory architecture (March), Crew Studio with tracing/deployment (July), and A2A task utilities. Open-source at v1.15.18 as of August 2026.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — Python framework; Cognitive Memory concept (consolidate/retrieve agent knowledge over time) is interesting but HID-188 already tracks episodic memory for AgentForge

source: arXiv 2606.30306 — Always-On Agents: Persistent Memory Survey
summary: Survey of persistent memory, state, and governance in LLM agents. Finds cross-session coherence (project conventions, prior fixes) critical for coding agents; cites MemRepair for hierarchical cross-session memory.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — directly related to executor prompt skill injection gap and HID-188 (episodic memory). Does not surface any new capability beyond what HID-188 tracks.

source: arXiv 2604.03515 — Inside the Scaffold: Coding Agent Architecture Taxonomy
summary: Source-code taxonomy of coding agents (SWE-agent, OpenHands, Codex CLI, OpenCode). Finds most have no cross-session persistence; OpenCode saves full session state in SQLite.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — confirms AgentForge's skill distillation approach is on the right track; SQLite session state is an interesting implementation pattern for HID-188 but doesn't change scope

source: arXiv 2609.05510 — Memory as Infrastructure: Reliability for Persistent Agent Memory
summary: Case study: 8 months of Claude Code development on one codebase using persistent memory with gating and per-hook telemetry. Most production-oriented paper found this run.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — practical implementation patterns for persistent memory. Gating + telemetry complement HID-188 and HID-163. No new theme beyond existing tracked issues.

source: arXiv 2607.20972 — Delivery Not Storage: Cue-Anchored Working Memory for Coding Agents
summary: Argues memory delivery at the harness level (cue-anchored injection at the right moment) matters more than storage design. Artifacts in linked Vectr repository.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — cue-anchored injection is exactly what AgentForge's promptRenderer does; paper may have patterns to improve skill injection timing. Relates to executor skill gap under HID-188.

summary: Karpathy coined 'Agentic Engineering' as successor to vibe coding: orchestrate agents as oversight layer. Also described a 'programmable layer' stack: agents, subagents, prompts, contexts, memory, modes, permissions, tools, plugins, skills, hooks, MCP.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — philosophical framing that aligns with AgentForge's existing design; no concrete implementation gap identified

source: Self-improving agent loop / Reflection pattern overview (2026 blogs)
summary: Generate-evaluate-revise reflection loops for agents; governance concerns around versioning, evaluation gates, approval, rollback. No specific new GitHub repo surfaced.
